utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Good morning, everybody. Good morning, Madam Registrar. Could you call the case, please.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours. This is case IT-05-88-T, The Prosecutor versus Vujadin Popovic, et al.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you. All the accused are present. Prosecution, today we have Mr. McCloskey and Mr. Vanderpuye. Amongst the Defence teams, I notice the absence of Ms. Tapuskovic, Mr. Nikolic, Mr. Bourgon, and Mr. Petrusic. All right the witness is already present. Good morning to you, Professor.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I hope you had a good rest. We are going to continue with your testimony today. I don't think we will finish today, but we'll make an effort to reduce it as much as possible. Mr. Lazarevic, he is in your good hands.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours. Good morning, everybody. I would first like to express my gratitude to my colleagues from the Prosecution for providing us with English translation of the document. Unfortunately, it hasn't still been released in the e-court system, but hard copies have been delivered. So, I think, we can safely proceed with the translation that we have right now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: We are talking of 4D192; aren't we? Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honours. Right.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning, Professor Bajagic.

utterances.speaker: MLADEN BAJAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Good morning.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Yesterday, when we adjourned, we were discussing document 4D129. That's tab number 10 in your binder.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated] ... read 192.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: For the record, today we are sitting pursuant to Rule 15 bis, only for the first session, due to an urgent matter that Mr. Justice Stole had to attend to.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Bajagic, do you have in front of you the set of rules on the internal organisation of MUP?

utterances.speaker: MLADEN BAJAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Let us now look at Article 10 which is on page 5 in the B/C/S version.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: This article lays down organisational units within MUP. Let us just look at the subtitle above Article 10.

utterances.speaker: MLADEN BAJAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: What is this about?

utterances.speaker: MLADEN BAJAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is the public security service.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Now, let us read Article 10. Can you tell me under item 1, it reads: "Special Brigade." Can you tell me something about this?

utterances.speaker: MLADEN BAJAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Article 10 lays down organisation units of the police administration and number 1, it's special brigade of police.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Can you tell us what detachments can we see underneath and the locations under?

utterances.speaker: MLADEN BAJAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Under subitems (a) to (d), it says that the special police brigade has five detachments located in Banja Luka, Bijeljina, Doboj, Sarajevo, and Trebinje.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Very well. And, now, in the previous paragraph of Article 10, functionally speaking, where the police special brigade was, part of which system it was?

utterances.speaker: MLADEN BAJAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In view of Article 7 and 10 of this set of rules, we see that the special police brigade is part of the public security service within the seat of the ministry.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: And, of course, the first sentence in Article 10 gives -- can you give us more details?

utterances.speaker: MLADEN BAJAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Within the police administration of this public security service, within the seat of the ministry.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Now, in order to clarify to the Chamber the difference between the organisation in functional terms and organisational terms, let us take an example of the special police brigade as set out in this set of rules, and the security services centre. Can you explain what was the relationship between these two units. Was there any hierarchical relationship or any other relationship?

utterances.speaker: MLADEN BAJAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: These two forms of organisations in the police, there was no hierarchical relationship. As we can see, the public security service is part of the ministry; and within it, there's police administration. At that time, one of its organisational parts was the special police brigade. On the other hand, the security services centre or the Public Security Centre was organised within the Ministry of Interior on a territorial basis. Therefore, there was no hierarchical relationship between the two; that is to say, no subordination or superiority. I presume that there were just some forms of cooperation because both these segments were part of the MUP.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: I have finished with this document for now, and now I would like us to move to the next period of the development of MUP of Republika Srpska; that's the period 1993-1995. You will find it under number 11 in your binder.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That's Exhibit 4D194; pages 5 and 6 in B/C/S, and pages 11 and 12 in English.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: We are talking about Article 61. First of all, let's say that this is the consolidated version of the constitution of Republika Srpska of the 31st of December 1992, and now we will move to Article 68. Do you have it in front of you?

utterances.speaker: MLADEN BAJAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Let us first look what Article 68 defines, the first sentence.

utterances.speaker: MLADEN BAJAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Let us now look at item 2. Can you give me your comment on this?

utterances.speaker: MLADEN BAJAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Under chapter 4 of this constitution, the first sentence of Article 68 reads that the following shall be regulated and provided by the republic; and under 2 it reads, defence and security of the republic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Let us now look at item 13.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That's on page 6 in B/C/S and on page 12 in English.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Item 13, what does it speak about?

utterances.speaker: MLADEN BAJAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It sets down the rights and obligations of the republic in terms of organising and defining responsibilities of state bodies.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Did that refer to MUP as well?

utterances.speaker: MLADEN BAJAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Definitely. MUP is one of the administrative organs. It is part of the state administration.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Can we now move to Articles 104 to 107.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] In the e-court system, that's on pages 8 and 9 in B/C/S, and page 18 in English.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Do you have it in front of you, Articles 104 to 107?

utterances.speaker: MLADEN BAJAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Can you tell us something more about chapter 7 where these articles are contained?

utterances.speaker: MLADEN BAJAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Chapter 7, entitled "Defence," regulates the right and duties; and Article 104 says that it's the right and the duty of all citizens to defend and protect the sovereignty and the constitutional order of Republika Srpska. That's Article 104.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Now, what about Article 105, tell us what it says?

utterances.speaker: MLADEN BAJAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Article 105 says that Republika Srpska has its army consisting of a standing and a reserve force, and that the standing army is composed of professional soldiers and those in the compulsory military service.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Can we just briefly discuss Article 106. Who commands the Army of Republika Srpska pursuant to Article 106?

utterances.speaker: MLADEN BAJAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Pursuant to Article 106, the Army of Republika Srpska both in peacetime and wartime is commanded by the president of the republic in accordance with the constitution.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: And now, briefly, what about Article 108 [as interpreted], what does it regulate?

utterances.speaker: MLADEN BAJAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Article 107 [as interpreted] regulates court marshals -- actually, military courts and military prosecutors.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Now, looking at this entire chapter regulating the issue of defence, can you tell me, is there any mention herein of MUP as one of the defence components?

utterances.speaker: MLADEN BAJAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: According to the provisions of chapter 7, the MUP is not understood in the traditional sense as part of the armed forces of Republika Srpska.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Let us now look at the next document which is the Law on Amendments to the Law. That's tab 12 in your binder. So this is the Law on Amendments to the Law on the Ministry of the Interior -- I'm sorry. I misspoke. This is the Law on Amendments to the Law on Internal Affairs, dated 30th December 1993.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That's 4D207 in e-court.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Let us first look at Article 1 of this law, which is, of course, and page 1 in B/C/S and as well in the English version in e-court.

utterances.speaker: MLADEN BAJAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Let's look at the law together. It's Article 3.

utterances.speaker: MLADEN BAJAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I've read it.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: And you can see yourself that in addition to the change in the title of the public security service into the public security sector, that the national security service changes into the public security service. Does this law bring any other more significant changes to the organisational structure?

utterances.speaker: MLADEN BAJAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As we can see in Articles 1 and 2 of this law, the former service becomes a sector. Further on, the national security service changes its name into the state security sector or department. We are talking about terminology here rather than any other more essential changes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Very well. And now I would like to move on to the next set of rules under number 4D212, which is the Law on Internal Affairs, dated 25 March 1994. In your binder, it is under tab 13.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I would like us to look at Article 3 of that law, which is on page 1 in the B/C/S version and on pages 2 and 3 in the English version.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: I would also like to look at the definition of Internal Affairs provided for by this law. Let's then look at Article 3 first. I apologise. Let me rephrase my question. Pursuant to Article 3, what would be the tasks and duties under the scope of Internal Affairs?

utterances.speaker: MLADEN BAJAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In the sense of this article, Internal Affairs imply the following: Duties and tasks of public security; duties and tasks of state security; and, under 3, duties and tasks related to some administrative affairs, such as personal identity card, personal name, maintaining the registry of the dead, and permanent residence of citizens, citizenship, vital registers, and so on and so forth.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Very well.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Let's move on to Article 24 in this law, which is in e-court on page 3 of B/C/S and on page 6 of the English version.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Could you please tell me what the article defines in terms of the police and its organisational units in a public security station?

utterances.speaker: MLADEN BAJAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: According to Article 24, police stations or public security stations shall have police stations established in addition to reserve police stations. In other words, in a public security station, there are police stations. And Article 24 also envisages that a police station can also have its departments outside of the station headquarters, and the organisational form of such a unit is the so-called station department.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Very well.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Let's move to Article 27 on the same page in B/C/S; and in English, it is on pages 6 and 7.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: I would like us to focus on certain tasks that are performed by the ministry headquarters. In Article 27, you see that it starts with the following words: "The ministry headquarters itself shall have the following duties and tasks." I would like to draw your attention to the second bullet point in this article. Could you please explain the meaning of the second bullet point?

utterances.speaker: MLADEN BAJAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Pursuant to Article 27 of this law, the ministry headquarters itself shall have the following duties and tasks; and pursuant to bullet point 2, these include to monitor, direct, and coordinate the work of the Public Security Centres and public security stations.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: We are still talking about Article 27. Let's move to the next column on your right-hand side. Let's first look at the third bullet point from the bottom, and could you please tell us what it defines?

utterances.speaker: MLADEN BAJAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: According to this, the ministry headquarters is in charge of preparing proposals for the organisation and the total number of the reserve police in the republic, as well as the criteria for the replenishment thereof.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Let's look at the next bullet point immediately thereafter. Can you please explain?

utterances.speaker: MLADEN BAJAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I'll try. According to this bullet point of Article 27, the ministry headquarters is in charge of activating the reserve police force in emergency situations pursuant to an order issued by the president of the republic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Can we please move on to the next bullet point.

utterances.speaker: MLADEN BAJAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. The next bullet point says that the ministry headquarters will procure weapons and requisite equipment for the active and reserve police from the allocated funds approved from the state budget, which means that the ministry headquarters is in charge of the global procurement of weapons and requisite equipment for the entire Ministry of the Interior and all its organisational units, and that would be my comment.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: And now let's move ton the next bullet point, and that will be my last about this article. Can you please comment upon the next bullet point in this article?

utterances.speaker: MLADEN BAJAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: According to this bullet point, the ministry headquarters is in charge of establishing programs of professional training and continuous education of the active and reserve police, i.e., members of the Ministry of the Interior, as well as other authorised official, and they also check their professional abilities and skills.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Let's then summarize. All these tasks and duties that we have just listed, who is in charge of those? Who is supposed to perform those tasks and duties?

utterances.speaker: MLADEN BAJAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: According to Article 27, we can see that all these duties and tasks are discharged by the ministry headquarters.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Very well then.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Let's look briefly at Article 30 of this law, which is on page 3 in B/C/S, and on pages 7 and 8 in the English version of this law in e-court.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: And let's please look at paragraph 1 which says: "Education of appropriate police units." Now that you've looked at Article 30, could you please tell us under whose authority would be this task?

utterances.speaker: MLADEN BAJAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The establishment of appropriate police units is under the authority of the ministry headquarters.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Let's move on to Article 31 of this law, which is on page 4 in B/C/S and on page 8 in the English version of this document in e-court.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Do you have Article 31 before you?

utterances.speaker: MLADEN BAJAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Who is in charge of the establishment of a unit or several units to carry out a particular duty or task pursuant to Article 31 of this law?

utterances.speaker: MLADEN BAJAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Pursuant to Article 31, the establishment of one or several units to carry out a particular duty or task is under the authority of the minister of the interior.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: And just one more question about this. The officer in charge of such a unit pursuant to Article 31, who is such an officer responsible to? Who does he report to?

utterances.speaker: MLADEN BAJAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The officer or officers of such unit or units report directly to the minister of the interior.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Very well. We will no longer need those documents for the time being. The next document that I would like us to look at is the set of rules on the internal organisation of the Ministry of the Interior, dated 1 April 1994. In your binder, it is under tab 14.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This is Exhibit number 4D144. We will start with page 2 in B/C/S, which is the same page in the English version of the document.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Let's first look at Article 2 of this book of rules or this regulation, paragraph 2 thereof.

utterances.speaker: MLADEN BAJAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Can you please read paragraph 2 for us?

utterances.speaker: MLADEN BAJAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It reads: "The minister's office is composed of the following component bureau for information: Under 1 -- under 2, Bureau for the Suppression of Illegal Trade of Drugs and Opiates; under 3, a helicopter unit; under 4, Directorate for Common Affairs; and, finally, under 5, special police brigade.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Very well. And now when we look at the provisions of Article 2, paragraph 2 of this set of rules in comparison with the previous regulation that we discussed, which is 4D192, would the solution under which the special police brigade is placed under the office of the minister, would that constitute a change, a material change to the law?

utterances.speaker: MLADEN BAJAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. From the moment this set of rules came into force, the special police brigade belonged to the office of the minister; and before that or up to then, before this set of rules was adopted, the special police brigade was part of the police administration, the public security service in the ministry headquarters. So there is a significant difference here.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Let's talk about the same article of this set of rules.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Let's look at the penultimate paragraph on page 5 in B/C/S or page 2 in the English version in e-court.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Could you please tell us what the provision you see here defines?

utterances.speaker: MLADEN BAJAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I apologise. Are we still talking about Article 2?

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Yes, we are.

utterances.speaker: MLADEN BAJAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: According to Article 2, the minister's office is in charge of the use of the special police brigade upon the minister's orders.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: We are talking about the penultimate and ultimate paragraph which is on page 4 in your document; penultimate paragraph and the last paragraph of Article 2, which is page 5 in e-court. But in your version, it's --

utterances.speaker: MLADEN BAJAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I can see it.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Do you see the penultimate paragraph of this article which starts with the words "special police brigade"?

utterances.speaker: MLADEN BAJAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I've found it.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Can you please now look at this paragraph?

utterances.speaker: MLADEN BAJAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: According to this paragraph, a special police brigade is in charge of discharging special tasks and duties which are as follows: Under 1, participation in combat; under 2, neutralizing sabotaging terrorist groups and individuals; under 3, restoring public peace and order where the two had been greatly violated; under 4, it performs defence preparations of the brigade's wartime composition; under 5, performs special training of the brigade members.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... we are looking at.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Your Honours, we are talking about Article 2, second to last paragraph of Article 2.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Could you please continue?

utterances.speaker: MLADEN BAJAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Let me continue. Monitors and proposes material of technical equipment of the brigade in the accordance with the latest world achievements in the field of arming technical instruments, police equipment; keeps prescribed records; and, finally, realises other assignments and tasks that are ordered to the brigade by the minister.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: And the first task of the special police brigade, what would it be according to this article?

utterances.speaker: MLADEN BAJAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: According to this provision of this article, the first and the foremost task of the special police brigade is to participate in combat.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: And now let's look at the last paragraph of this article. Do you have it in front of you? Can you tell me something about it? What does it define and set out?

utterances.speaker: MLADEN BAJAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The last paragraph of this article defines the overall organisation of the special police brigade, and it says that the special police brigade includes in its complement, first, the brigade command, and, second, special police detachments. Then it enumerates --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Sorry. Could you check whether we have English translation of that part. I have difficulty.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: I apologise. I will check, if Your Honours can bear with me for one minute.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour, I was just advised by my co-counsel that is he looking at it. I think we do have the translation in the e-court system.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Are we looking at the correct page now?

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: It should be -- it's the following page in English. It should be page 3, I think.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: We are talking about Article 6?

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Article 2, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Page 3 is --

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honours. It's a partial translation, not whole document is translated, only the relevant part that we intended to use with this witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay. Let's proceed. Thank you, Judge Kwon.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated]

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone please.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Dr. Bajagic, relative to the previous rule book, has the number of detachments increased in this one?

utterances.speaker: MLADEN BAJAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The number of detachments of special police is increased by two. The previous rule book envisaged five, and this rule book envisages the existence of seven special police detachments; namely, the Sarajevo Detachment, Banja Luka, Doboj, Bijeljina, and Prijedor detachments that were previously in existence, and two new ones: Sekovici and Bilice.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Can we now move on to Article 57 of these rules.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It's in page 7 in B/C/S and 5 in English.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Can you tell us what does Article 57 govern?

utterances.speaker: MLADEN BAJAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: According to Article 57 of these rules, the headquarters of the ministry is to be set up in case a state of war is proclaimed, and that headquarters of staff, rather, is to be managed by the minister.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Go on, please.

utterances.speaker: MLADEN BAJAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The article goes on to specify who the staff consists of, and it enumerates the minister, deputy minister, various heads of the public security department and the state security department, the commander of the special police brigade, the brigade command, and the commander of the PJP.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Could you look at the last paragraph in this article. What is understood under the term used here, "police forces"?

utterances.speaker: MLADEN BAJAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Pursuant to this article, police forces consist of members of the special police brigade and members of the active and reserve police.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: All right. Let us now go back to Article 6.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It is to be found on page 6 in the e-court system in B/C/S, and in English, it's on page 3.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Do you have Article 6 before you?

utterances.speaker: MLADEN BAJAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Can you tell us what are the various organisational units according to this article that existed within the public security department?

utterances.speaker: MLADEN BAJAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As we can see from Article 6, the Public Security Department or Sector included the following organisational units: 1, the police administration; 2, crime prevention administration; 3, border affairs and foreigners administration; 4, inspectorate for firefighting and preventative technical protection; 5, analysis and information administration; 6, administration for communications and encryption; 7, administration of legal affairs; 8, duty operation centre; 9, centre for breeding, training, and usage of service dogs and horses; and, 10, public security centres.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: All right. Let us move on to Article 15.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Those are pages 10 and 11 in B/C/S, and in English, it's 3 and 4.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Based on this article, can you tell us which organisational units form the police administration?

utterances.speaker: MLADEN BAJAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The organisational units of the police administration as part of the public security sector are: 1, police squad; 2, police station, securing physical persons and facilities; 3, police station for railway station security -- for railway security; 3 [as interpreted], department for road traffic security; and, finally, a section for defence affairs and special operational activities.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Can we dwell for awhile on the section for defence affairs and special operational activities. Here, in this Article 15, under this subheading midway down the paragraph, it says: "Proposes formations and organisations of separate police units, PJP." Is that the case according to this article?

utterances.speaker: MLADEN BAJAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Pursuant to this article, the section for defence affairs and special operational activities which belongs to the police administration is responsible for drafting proposals concerning formations and organisation of separate police units, PJP.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Just to remind ourselves, let us go back to Article 57.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That's page 7 in B/C/S, and 5 in English in e-court.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Now, in your comments, you mentioned also the role of the PJP commander. Let me ask you, before this rule book was adopted, did such a function, did such a position, PJP commander, exist?

utterances.speaker: MLADEN BAJAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: To the best of my knowledge, this is the first reference to the position of PJP commander.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: All right. We won't be needing this document any longer, for the time being.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Mr. Lazarevic, I'd like to personally have the full translation of Article 2 and Article 56 and preceding articles which you deal with the PJP, if you could make sure.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. We'll request the full translation, and as soon as it arrive, it will be uploaded in e-court.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Bajagic, let us move on to a set of rules that were valid in July 1995 regarding the organisation and powers of the MUP in July 1995.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] They are to be found in e-court as 4D413.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: In your binder, it's tab 15. I will give a reference now and we'll move on slowly through these laws: The laws on the application of the Law on Government in Republika Srpska during state of war or immediate threat of war; second, law on the application of the Law on Ministries during immediate threat of war or state of war; three, the law on the application of the Law on Defence during the immediate threat of war or state of war; four, law on the application of the Law on the Army during immediate threat of war or state of war; and, five, the law on the application of the Law on Internal Affairs during immediate threat of war or state of war. The first law that I would like to look at and hear your comments is the Law on the Government of Republika Srpska during the immediate threat of war or state of war. That's Exhibit 4D413; your tab 15.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We want Article 3, paragraph 2. It's on page 1 in B/C/S, and page 2 in English.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Now, having looked at Article 3, tell me, what is the purpose of these provisions? In which way do they lay the framework for the functioning of the ministry during the immediate threat of war.

utterances.speaker: MLADEN BAJAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Article 3 says that the government of Republika Srpska exercises its constitutional and legal functions through ministries, district, commissioners offices, local authorities, and war presidencies of municipalities. By virtue of this very law, it's Article 3, the government of Republika Srpska exercises its powers through republic ministries including the one on the interior.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: The next law I want to look at is the Law on Defence during immediate threat of war or state of war.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That's page 3 in both B/C/S and English, 4D413.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Your tab 15. First of all, one general question: Can you tell us, does this law change the role of the MUP compared to its peacetime role pursuant to Article 2.

utterances.speaker: MLADEN BAJAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Are we talking about the law on the application of the Law on Defence?

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Precisely.

utterances.speaker: MLADEN BAJAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Article 2 says that the armed forces of Republika Srpska shall consist of the Army of Republika Srpska, one; and, two, the units of the Ministry of the Interior of Republika Srpska. It's a significant change, if you wanted my comments, because for the first time units of the MUP are mentioned as a component of the armed forces.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: My question is: Is this about the entire structure of the Ministry of the Interior or just its units?

utterances.speaker: MLADEN BAJAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The law on the application of the Law on Defence in immediate threat of war and state of war is very clear and precise. It refers to the units of the Ministry of the Interior.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: And the Ministry of the Interior as an administrative body, does it continue to operate with all its powers regardless of the fact that an immediate threat of war or state of war has been declared?

utterances.speaker: MLADEN BAJAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The circumstances of immediate threat of war and state of war imply a certain expansion of the powers and role of the Ministry of the Interior; but in any case, the ministry continues to discharge its functions normally within its jurisdiction just as in peacetime. It continues to be engaged in protecting law and order, the personal security of citizens and their property, crime prevention, et cetera.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: I would now like to look at 4D416 [as interpreted]. It's your tab 73. I think it's the second binder.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: It was the wrong document, I notice, in the e-court. It's 461.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Bajagic, do you see the document?

utterances.speaker: MLADEN BAJAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: First, let me ask you this: You did not draft this diagram yourself?

utterances.speaker: MLADEN BAJAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I didn't.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Have you seen it before?

utterances.speaker: MLADEN BAJAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, while I was preparing my report and before I came to this courtroom.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: One moment. I notice Mr. Borovcanin. Do you wish to consult with your lawyer, Mr. Borovcanin?

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: I apologise. We have two different schematics here; one on the right and the one on the left.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: No, no. I noticed him trying to attract your attention.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: That's what Mr. Borovcanin wanted to indicate, I think.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you. Let's proceed then.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: It's 461. The one on the left side is right, but on the right side is not correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'm sorry. Can we continue now.

utterances.speaker: MLADEN BAJAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No problem.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Your Honours, I believe that the B/C/S version should be in the e-court system, too. I don't know what seems to be the problem.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. We can proceed.

utterances.speaker: MLADEN BAJAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I actually don't need it.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Can you tell me what this diagram represents?

utterances.speaker: MLADEN BAJAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This diagram represents the organisation of armed forces of Republika Srpska according to the applicable laws.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: This diagram pursuant to the law on the implementation of the Law on Defence in the state of imminent threat of war and state of war, the first box says: "Armed Forces of Republika Srpska."

utterances.speaker: MLADEN BAJAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, Armed Forces of the RS.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Beneath it is what?

utterances.speaker: MLADEN BAJAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The box beneath it says: "Commander in Chief, President of the RS," and that is according to the law. Next to him, we have Supreme Command, and there are two lines, one going to the Supreme Command made up of, naturally, in addition to the commander in chief, RS, vice-president, the president of the national assembly of Republika Srpska, the prime minister of the RS, the minister of defence and the minister of the interior.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Let's move now to the next level. Tell me, what does it represent?

utterances.speaker: MLADEN BAJAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It represents two main components of the armed forces of the RS pursuant to the law on the implementation of the Law on Defence in an immediate threat of war and a state of war. There's the Main Staff and the police forces staff; and underneath, according to the law, we have the RS army and MUP units.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Very well. I think we have finished with this document. Let us now look on the law on the implementation of Law on Internal Affairs during an imminent threat of war and state of war. That's Exhibit 4D413, and it's tab 15 in your binder.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] First of all, let us look at paragraphs 1 and 2 of Article 4. It's on page 4 in B/C/S, and on page 9 in English.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. Pursuant to Article 4, the ministry [Realtime transcript read in error "minister"] is considered to be a part of the armed forces of RS, and its forces are managed or controlled by the president of the republic as the commander in chief?

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: For the transcript, it's on page 21, line 22. Instead of "the minister," it says "the ministry." It should read "the ministry." It seems to be that there is one more correction. It should read "Answer" instead of "Question." This was not the question; this was the answer.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: When the mistakes are minor, let's leave them for later. You can see them with the -- otherwise, let's stick to corrections that need to be made immediately; otherwise, one could get complete misunderstanding of what is going on. So let's proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Very well, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Bajagic, we were talking about paragraphs 1 and 2 of Article 4, and you responded by saying that the ministry was considered part of the armed forces. Can you continue where you left off, and that is paragraph 2 of Article 4.

utterances.speaker: MLADEN BAJAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Paragraph 2 of Article 4 of this law says that the Ministry of the Interior is responsible and in charge of carrying out the orders of the president of the republic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: In your opinion, what is the significance of these provisions?

utterances.speaker: MLADEN BAJAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The Law on Internal Affair, or the law on the implementation of this law, for the first time clearly defines the position of the ministry at a time when a state is in an immediate threat of war or at war. In the basic law, the ministries for the first time defined as a part of the armed forces of Republika Srpska.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Let's look now at article 5 of this law.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It's on the same page in B/C/S, and on pages 9 and 10 in English.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: During your testimony, we already said that this defines the measures that the ministry can undertake during an imminent threat of war or the state of war. How would you assess the powers vested in the MUP compared to those in peacetime?

utterances.speaker: MLADEN BAJAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think that, yesterday, we said or discussed almost all of these administrative actions envisaged by this law. We even said how completely different powers these are or whether some of these existed before but were only amended and altered. But, in my judgement, it is only natural to see the expansion of powers of all participants in the security system, including the Ministry of the Interior, when it comes to an immediate threat of war or a state of war.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Very well. So far, we spoke about different laws and bylaws governing the position and the structure of the RS MUP. In order for the Honourable Chamber to be able to follow better these issues, let us now look at a number of charts. Let's first look at the one attached to your expert report, and it's tab 16 in your binder?

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That's chart 1A, and that's 4D448.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: I think we have the right document both in e-court and before you. Can you please now explain this chart to me. First of all, this is a chart depicting the organisation of MUP of the Republika Srpska in July 1995; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MLADEN BAJAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Let us now start with this top box which says "The Ministry of Interior." How is it being divided according to this chart?

utterances.speaker: MLADEN BAJAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: According to this chart, an attempt was made to portray the organisation of MUP that existed in July in 1995, and that was according to the laws in place at the time. There are actually three levels of organisation here. As we can see on the right-hand side of this chart, it says level 1, level 2, and level 3. Level 1 implies how the ministry is organised within its very seat which, conditionally speaking, has several global organisational segments. In addition to the public security department and the state security department, on the left-hand side, you can also see a number of units. That's the office of the minister, the service for public information, education centre, and the special police brigade. Also, there is the finance administration and personnel administration. These are organisational units that exist at the seat of the ministry. In addition to that, as you can see from the chart, there are individual administrations as organisational parts of the public security department, and I can enumerate them, if necessary.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Please go ahead.

utterances.speaker: MLADEN BAJAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Within the public security department, there's the police administration, the criminal investigation police administration, the administration for analysis, IT, and automatic data processing, the administration for communications and crypto protection, the administration for legal affairs and aliens, and, finally, the firefighting inspectorate and for technical prevention.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Let me just ask you this: In this chart, you did not elaborate any further the state security department; this is more to do with the public security department.

utterances.speaker: MLADEN BAJAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. As you can see, the line going from the Ministry of the Interior goes to the public security department, and the state security department was not the subject of my analysis, it was not in my remit. That's why I put it like this, but I thought it was necessary to show it that it was part of the Ministry of the Interior.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Okay. We spoke now about level 1, and you said this refers to the seat of the ministry. What is level 2 in your chart?

utterances.speaker: MLADEN BAJAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As we can see, level 2 after we mentioned the seat are actually regional organisational units of the MUP established on a territorial principle. We have public security centres at the second level. And in brackets in this chart, it just says that there were ten of them, one to ten. And in the appendices you can find precisely which centres these were. So this is as far as level 2 goes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Can you tell us something about level 3 now?

utterances.speaker: MLADEN BAJAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Concerning level 3, we can see that these are organisational units of MUP at an even lower level and these are public security stations. In any case, there were more of them than the centres because public security stations generally coincided with the territory of municipals; therefore, we see this territorial principle.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Very well. I think we have finished with this chart; and before the break, can we please look at the next document. I suppose we shall have ample time to discuss it. That's chart 1B attached to your report. And as far as I understand, it derives from chart 1A.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That's 4D449.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Tab 16 in your binder.

utterances.speaker: MLADEN BAJAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I have it before me.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Just bear with me for a moment, we are awaiting for both versions to appears in e-court. Let me check if they are correct. Yes, they are. Can you explain now explain for the Trial Chamber what the sketches represents. I believe that it derives from the schematic 1A. Could you please explain the schematic 1B that we have in front of us?

utterances.speaker: MLADEN BAJAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The schematic 1B which is in front of us is a derivative from the left part of the previous schematic. In order to provide a more detailed explanation of the organisation of the Ministry of the Interior and its headquarters what it is envisaged to do under the law. The Ministry of the Interior had two offices in Bijeljina and Pale. It says here that the Ministry of the Interior in the headquarters has a minister, a deputy minister, advisors, chiefs, directors and other organisational views, as well as the chief of the police force.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Could you please slow down a little. We have problems with the transcript?

utterances.speaker: MLADEN BAJAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I apologise.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Can you please repeat what you just said?

utterances.speaker: MLADEN BAJAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The Ministry of the Interior in its headquarters has minister; a deputy minister; ministers advisors, five of them to be more precise; chiefs of internal control inspectorate, one person; five chief inspectors; and chief police force staff.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Can we move on please.

utterances.speaker: MLADEN BAJAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. And, ultimately, in addition to that, the ministry in its headquarters has the minister's office, public information service, finance directorate, personnel directorate, and special police brigade, which means that the left part of the first schematic has only been enlarged in this schematic. Nothing else. We also see on the right-hand side of this schematic only the titles of the public security department and the state security department in the squares?

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Very well. Just one more question, please in this regard. Here there's reference to the chief of police force staff. Would that be the minister himself?

utterances.speaker: MLADEN BAJAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. It wouldn't be the minister of the interior, no. This is just the position that exists and has been envisaged in the headquarters of the Ministry of the Interior.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Well, to develop further, and I don't believe we'll be able to finish with his answer in five minutes. So maybe it's time to have a break right now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay. We'll have a break now, 25 minutes. How much longer do you think you will be?

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Well, I believe that I will take the rest of the day, and, probably, I must say by looking at the way I'm progressing, probably first session tomorrow.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: So that will be in excess of the six hours that you indicated. Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Well, slightly.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Twenty-five minutes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, let's resume. Mr. Lazarevic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Dr. Bajagic, we left it off considering the schematic 4D449. I would like to move on to the next schematic in your expert report to tab 16 on page 3.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It is 1C; and in e-court, it's 4D450.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: It arises from the title of the scheme that this is the organisation of the Ministry of the Interior in its headquarters as it was in July 1995?

utterances.speaker: MLADEN BAJAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Could you please give us your comment of this schematic?

utterances.speaker: MLADEN BAJAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: With regard to the previous schematic, this also provides the schematic of the Ministry of the Interior of the Republika Srpska in July 1995, with a special emphasis on the public security department and again on the left side, the exclamation, i.e., the overview of the organisational units that belong to the headquarters itself. We can see that in the Ministry of the Interior, there is the public security department with six squares depicting organisational units of the public security departments -- or rather, administrations or directorates. I can go on and enumerate them. Public security department has the following organisational units: Under 1, the police administration; under 2, the administration of the crime prevention police; under 3, the administration for analysis IT, and automatic processing, data processing; under 4, the administration for communications and encryption; under 5, administration for legal affairs and foreigners; and, finally, under 6, fire protection and technical protection directorate.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: I apologise. There are two more directorates or administrations, but they are not within the public security department in your schematic. Why?

utterances.speaker: MLADEN BAJAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. Just like in the schematic that I entitled 1B, which is a different scheme from this one, I said that in addition to the ministers office, the information office, and special police brigade, the MUP in the headquarters also has the directorate for material and equipment - this is the square on the left-hand side - and the director for personnel. These do not belong to the public security department, but, rather, to the Ministry of the Interior and its headquarters.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Obviously, in your schematic, we can also see that the special brigade is also there.

utterances.speaker: MLADEN BAJAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. You can see it in the schematic that the special police brigade belongs to the Ministry of the Interior in its headquarters.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Thank you very much. We will no long need in document. Can we now look at the following schematic that you have drafted and attached to your expert report. You will find it under tab 16 on page 4.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This is 1D, schematic 1D; and in e-court, it is 4D451. [In English] We provided hard copies, just in order for everyone to follow. [Interpretation] Very well. I believe we have both documents in e-court, both in B/C/S and English. They are identical.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Could you now please give us a brief outline of the organisational scheme of the public security department?

utterances.speaker: MLADEN BAJAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This schematic provides a detailed overview of the organisational structure of the public security department. Immediately below the long square depicting the words "public security department," you can see listed the chief of public security department, his deputy and assistant, followed by chief inspector, as well as the technical personnel. Let me not go through each and every one of them. And, also, within the management part of the public security department, we also have the duty service and finance section. You will find those on your left-hand side, the left-hand side of the page.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Very well then. And, now, please, could you explain the second row of squares?

utterances.speaker: MLADEN BAJAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As we have already said it, the police directorate has six particular directors. We can see that the police directorate, which is emphasized in bold; then criminal police directorate; analytics and information directorate; communications and crypto-protection directorate; legal and foreigners directorate; and fire protection and technical prevention inspectorate.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: We already had all those in the previous schematic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I should apologise. We have been warned that you are talking too fast.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I apologise. I will repeat. The police directorate, criminal police directorate, analytics and information directorate, communications and crypto-protection directorate, legal and foreigners directorate, fire protection and technical protection inspectorate.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Very well. And now I would kindly ask you to explain the further subdivision that you depict in the schematic?

utterances.speaker: MLADEN BAJAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As you can see in the schematic, a special emphasis has been placed on the police directorate. It is in the bold square, and we can see how it is actually organised. Immediately below the square, you can see that there are some key figures such as chief and his deputy, as well as the commander of special police units or PJPs.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: In accordance with this schematic, therefore - and I believe that it was based on the regulations that you analysed and that we have already discussed - the commander of the special police units is attached to the police directors?

utterances.speaker: MLADEN BAJAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. And, of course, the schematic has been drafted based on the laws and rules, i.e., bylaws that accompany those laws.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Very well. Can you now please continue explaining the schematic ever the police directorate?

utterances.speaker: MLADEN BAJAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. The police director ate also has the following organisational units: Under 1, sector of state border affairs, general police section, road traffic safety section, and defence affairs section.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Very well. And just let's wrap it up, there is the general police section here. Could you please explain the two organisational units underneath?

utterances.speaker: MLADEN BAJAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Underneath, it is says that the general police section within the police directorate, there is police station for securing persons and facilities for securing persons and the rail traffic safety police station.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Very well. I believe that we will no longer need this document, and I would like to call up the following schematic. In your binder, you will find it on page 9, tab 16.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This is a schematic number 6 and the number of this exhibit is 4D456.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I apologise. I just wanted to check that we have these documents in e-court -- actually, that we have the corresponding B/C/S and English versions.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Can you tell me now, this chart represent the organisation of the Zvornik Public Security Centre. Can you tell me, first, what is the top part of the chart represent? What do these diagonal boxes represent?

utterances.speaker: MLADEN BAJAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is an organisational chart of one of the public security centres, the one in Zvornik, which in view of the first chart that we saw today belongs to the second level of organisation in the MUP. We said that there were ten public security centres and the Zvornik centre is highlighted here in this bold box, and diagonally from it are the names of other public security centres that existed at the time.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Can you just tell us what these centres were, their names?

utterances.speaker: MLADEN BAJAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I will just read them from left to right, or from top to bottom. That's Banja Luka, Bijeljina, Doboj, Drvar, Zvornik, Mrkonic Grad, Prijedor, Sarajevo, Srbinje, and Trebinje Public Security Centres.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Let us now move on to the Zvornik Public Security Centre, and can you explain to us the organisational chart of this particular centre?

utterances.speaker: MLADEN BAJAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Here it goes. In addition to its two executives, that is, the chief and the deputy chief of the Zvornik Public Security Centre, there are also seven departments and sections within the centre, and that applies to other centres as well. I'm going to name them from left to right: Number 1 is police department; number 2 is crime prevention department; number 3, administration for personnel and foreigners; next to it is the fire protection section; number 5, communications and crypto-protection department; number 6, analytics and automatic data processing department; and number 5 [as interpreted], finance department.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Let me ask you this: With regard to the police department as one of the seven department within the Zvornik Public Security Centre, can you tell us the positions listed in the box underneath?

utterances.speaker: MLADEN BAJAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: We can see that this has been specially highlighted here in this box, that it has the police department chief within the public security centre, the PJP commander, or the commander of special police units; and these are probably these two subsections for defence preparation organisation and mobilisation, and police work improvement and monitoring subsection.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Very well. Therefore, according to this chart, the PJP commander at the Zvornik Public Security Centre is within the police department; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MLADEN BAJAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Let us now move on with further explanation of this chart. The next, so to speak, lower level of organisation represents what?

utterances.speaker: MLADEN BAJAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I referred you to the first chart when I said that there were three levels, and the public security sections represent the third level of organisation and these are regional units. Within the public security centre, there are, as we can see, five public security stations; namely, Bratunac, Vlasenici, Milici, Sekovici Public Security Stations, and the Skelani Police Station. They are organised according to the territorial principle, and they are at a lower organisational level. And, of course, within the public security centre itself, there are two police stations as part of their internal organisation. These are the Zvornik Police Station and the Road Safety Police Station of Zvornik. The Zvornik Police Station had general jurisdiction within the centre.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Can I now ask you, please, to tell us the following: In this last box, which is made up of dotted lines, you made some comments about the Zvornik Public Security Centre, PJPs. Can you explain that in detail?

utterances.speaker: MLADEN BAJAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In light of the organisation and the area of responsibility [as interpreted] of the PJP, and with regard to the second and third level of organisational MUP, we see that the PJP units of the Zvornik centre are made up of six companies. That refers to all the public security stations and police stations combined, and that each company is made up of the personnel from all police stations or public security stations. These are actually members of all police stations and public security stations that gather together occasionally, and they constitute a provisional unit, and, in terms of formation, they constitute a separate unit. They are actually a formation at the level of a public security centre.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... problem with transcript, I was just advised by my legal assistant. It's page 34 and it's on line 7. It speaks about the "area of responsibility" of the PJP. He was speaking -- he never actually mentioned any "zone of responsibility" of the PJP. He was talking about "territorial principle" of establishing PJP, not the "zone of responsibility."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you. Do you confirm that, Professor?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I can repeat. The police stations vis-a-vis the public security centre implies occasional gathering of PJPs. It stems from the territorial organisation of these two levels; that is, public security stations, police stations, and public security centres.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. I think this is clarified. Perhaps the interpretation was somewhat ambiguous.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Let us now move on to a separate part of your expert report, and it deals with the special police brigade --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Mr. Lazarevic, if you could ask the witness to clarify the difference of SJB and PS in this schematic, police station and public security station.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour, I will gladly do that.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Bajagic, you have heard what Honourable Judge Kwon said. Can you please explain the difference between public security stations and police stations according to your chart?

utterances.speaker: MLADEN BAJAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: A public security station is at level three of the organisational chart of minister. They are regional units set up on a territorial principle, and they are in charge of duties that involve such tasks as maintaining law and order, general jurisdiction of police like prevention of crime, et cetera. Police stations, however, are smaller in size than the public security stations, and they are predominantly involved in general police work. These are uniform policemen discharging general duties and tasks.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Just as an additional clarification, I'm sorry, I can probably assist the Honourable Judge to follow this better.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Let me ask you this: Does this depend on whether we are talking about municipalities or some smaller places?

utterances.speaker: MLADEN BAJAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This refers to smaller places. I can add this, and this will help you make a distinction better: Public security stations also have subsections for administrative actions; whereas, police stations don't have those.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: You are welcome.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could the witness please speak away from the microphone. He is too close for the interpreters.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Bajagic, let us move on now to a separate section of your report that deals with the special police brigade or police, as it had been originally called --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's correction: Militia, as it had originally been called.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Explain, please, how the special police brigade of the Ministry of Interior of the Republika Srpska was established?

utterances.speaker: MLADEN BAJAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Within the Ministry of the Interior of the Socialist Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina --

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Obviously, this was not my question. What I can read --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: [Overlapping speakers] ... explain how the ministry of the Republika Srpska was established.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: No. I was referencing to the special police brigade of the MUP of Republika Srpska. I mean, this is really something that I asked the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you. Professor, the interpreters have kindly asked you to keep away from the microphone as much as you can because your voice is --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: [Overlapping speakers] ... strong enough.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yeah. Thank you. Mr. Lazarevic, you have put your question and the professor can now answer it.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I apologise.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Professor, could you please tell us about the beginnings of the special brigade of the MUP of Republika Srpska. How did it come to be?

utterances.speaker: MLADEN BAJAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: We have to bear in mind the fact that in the Ministry of the Interior of the Socialist Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina, up to 1992, there was a similar unit and it was known as a special police detachment. When the ministry broke up and when the Ministry of the Interior first of the Serbian Republic Bosnia-Herzegovina and then of Republika Srpska were created and encompassed the pre-war special police detachment, this would be the nucleus of the future special police brigade, later to be known the special police brigade of the Republika Srpska MUP.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: All right. Let us now look at the next document in your binder. It's tab 17.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] In e-court, it's 4D523, and it's a three-page document. Let us look at page 1, please. All right. Now we have it in e-court, both B/C/S and English.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Can you tell me first in the upper left corner. It's the Serbian republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina, Ministry of the Interior, Sarajevo. Can you tell us what CSB means?

utterances.speaker: MLADEN BAJAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Security services centre. We know that from the acronyms, and then it goes on to specify special unit, police squad [as interpreted].

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Can you tell us what kind of document this is?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's correction: It's not police squad, it's police detachment.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This is a list of employees who were employees in May 1992 at the special unit of the police detachment. The list is for the down payment on salaries paid out for that month, and we see the names of the members of that unit.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we look at the last page of this document both in B/C/S and in English.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Can you tell me the total number of members of the special unit as it was then?

utterances.speaker: MLADEN BAJAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: We see it was 170 members of the special police detachment.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: From all the documents and information that you had at your disposal in writing your expert report, would you say that this number increased during the war in Bosnia from 1992 through 1995?

utterances.speaker: MLADEN BAJAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Of course, it increased, also, in view of the changed position and responsibilities and duties that were assigned to the special police, in view of the complexity of their work, the needs that arose, the number of members gradually increased.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: In order to better understand the legislative framework in which the special police brigade operated, I'd like to go through various rule books and regulations that governed the powers and responsibilities of the special police brigade within the MUP of Republika Srpska.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We have already had occasion, and I'd only like to remind the Chamber of the Law on Internal Affairs, 4D172; and the organisation of the ministry in immediate threat of war and state of war dated September 1992, that's 4D192.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: These laws envisaged the special brigade as part of the ministry in its seat. It was also in the centre of public security as we saw in your organogram. In your tab 10, you will find the document I want to look at now.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It's 4D192, Article 23. It's page 10 in B/C/S, and the pages that are important in English are 7 and 8; in fact, page 8 in e-court, the very beginning. [In English] I apologise. It's not in e-court, it's in the draft translation that we provided. It showed up in the e-court.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We are now looking at the beginning of Article 23, item 1, where it says "special police brigade."

utterances.speaker: MLADEN BAJAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: It's best to proceed this way: What were the responsibilities and duties of the special police brigade?

utterances.speaker: MLADEN BAJAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Pursuant to Article 23 of these rules, item 1, the special police brigade performs the following duties and tasks: 1, detection, apprehension, and liquidation of sabotage terrorist groups and individuals; 2, restoring law and order after serious violations and disturbances; 3, providing physical security to designated persons and facilities; 4, participating in the adoption and implementation of the defence plan of the ministry in its seat; 5, performing defence preparations of the combat complement of the brigade; 6, performing professional training of brigade members; 7, monitoring and proposing the equipment of the brigade with materiel and equipment; and, 8, keeping the records that are envisaged; and, 9, performing other duties and responsibilities ordered to it.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: When it says here "performing other duties pursuant to orders in view of the war in Bosnia," what are these other duties?

utterances.speaker: MLADEN BAJAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: When analysing the entire legislative framework and the bylaws governing the responsibilities and powers of the special police brigade, and bearing in mind the events especially in the state of war, it was my judgement that this means participation in combat activities.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Just one more question in this regard: Having reviewed all these tasks and having told us that this is also a reference to performing combat activities, which aspect of activity was dominant for the special police brigade, especially during the war in Bosnia?

utterances.speaker: MLADEN BAJAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: We see from this a list of tasks of the special police brigade, detection, apprehension, et cetera; but, certainly, participation in combat activities became one of the dominant duties of the special police brigade over time.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Very well. I'd like to move on to the next document, please. In your binder, it's tab 16, page 5.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It's 4D452.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: I am sorry. I'll put my question to you. I'm just waiting for the document in e-court. Do you have it in front of you now? It's the organogram of the special police brigade. We've just discussed the rule on the internal organisation of the MUP in immediate threat of war, circumstances in the state of war dating back to 1993, and now I'd like you to explain about the structure of the special police brigade under the new rules.

utterances.speaker: MLADEN BAJAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: May I begin now?

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Go ahead.

utterances.speaker: MLADEN BAJAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The special police brigade, under the rules in effect at the time, had a command within which, as we see on the left-hand side, there was a company for dealing with special jobs, a company for securing facilities, and a logistical unit.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: May I just put a few questions to you. What were the tasks of the company for special or extraordinary tasks?

utterances.speaker: MLADEN BAJAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Those were peculiar tasks and affairs, as stated here, concerning the special police brigade, combat against sabotage terrorist groups and so on, establishing special regimen of traffic around specially protected installations, et cetera. That's one of the basic tasks. I stated that in greater detail in my report. I'm trying to find it now.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: I don't want to dwell on it too long --

utterances.speaker: MLADEN BAJAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Hostage situations, aircraft hijackings, really special or specialised tasks that concern the special police brigade.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: I'd look to look at the right-hand side of your organogram where it states "police detachments."

utterances.speaker: MLADEN BAJAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. That's the other part of the organisational structure of the special police brigade, and we can see that these are police detachments of which there were five at the time under those rules. Those were Banja Luka, Bijeljina, Doboj, Sarajevo, and Trebinje Detachments.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Just for Your Honours' information, this schematic was made pursuant to 4D519, for which we don't have a translation, so we haven't used it in the course of the examination. But as soon as the translation of this document arrives, it will be available in e-court.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] In your report, para 130 of your report --

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
