utterances.text: [Interpretation] It's 4D499; page 39 in e-court in B/C/S, and page 40 in English.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: -- I read that the seats or basis of the special detachments of the police coincided with the security services centre. Did this fact affect command and management jurisdiction in any way? Could these special police detachments be commanded, for instance, by the chief of the security services centre, for instance?

utterances.speaker: MLADEN BAJAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. All police detachments which belong, as we know, to the special police brigade, were directly subordinated to the command of the special police brigade; thus, the chief of the security service centre, or the public security centre, could not give any orders or have any relation of superiority towards the police detachments.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: All right. Now I'd only like to sum up briefly because we've already had occasion to analyse the law amending the Law on Internal Affairs, dated 30th December 1993. We've spoken about it. It was 4D207 in tab 12. We talked about the renaming of the services into public security sector and state security sector, and the renaming of "milicija" into "policija." At that time as far as the special police brigade is concerned, did that law bring any other change except for the name?

utterances.speaker: MLADEN BAJAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, not at that time. A change did occur, but later.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Fine. Now I'd like to show you another document. In your binder it's tab 18, and it's the rules on the job specification within the Ministry of the Interior, dated 5 October 1994.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] And in e-court, it's page 5 in B/C/S, in page 2 in English. This is an unofficial translation that we've been able to provide. Let us look at Article 2.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: I am sorry. I didn't mention it before, but it's your page 5. Just above that -- sorry. Just below that is Article 3.

utterances.speaker: MLADEN BAJAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: 4D145. It's page 3 in the e-court in English.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Do you have that before you?

utterances.speaker: MLADEN BAJAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Do you see the title, "Special Police Brigade"?

utterances.speaker: MLADEN BAJAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Can you please explain the definitions of this provision?

utterances.speaker: MLADEN BAJAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This provision of Article 2 defines the activities and tasks for which the special police brigade is in charge, and they are listed.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Very well. I'm interested in the second paragraph within the subtitle "Special Police Brigade." Look at the second paragraph where it says: "In it's composition," and so on and so forth.

utterances.speaker: MLADEN BAJAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I can see it. It says here: "In its composition, the special police brigade contains a command of the brigade and special police detachments," and a list of six is given -- actually, seven special police detachments are listed. In other words, the number is increased by two with respect to the original organisation. This is the kind of change that happened.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Very well. And now I would just like to show something else which is not that important, but, still, I would like to show some other relevant parts of this paragraph.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Let's look at the job specification, which is on pages 11 through 13 and page 8 in the English version in e-court, and also page 9 of the English version.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Let us just say that different positions in the brigade are mentioned here.

utterances.speaker: MLADEN BAJAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: And pages 13 to 17 refer to the job specification of jobs in the special police detachment; wouldn't that be correct?

utterances.speaker: MLADEN BAJAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. We can see that this is a list or job specification both in the brigade command as well as in the detachments.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Very well. We will not dwell upon this document because it's rather self-explanatory. What I'd like to look at now is tab 16 in your expert report, which is your page 6, schematic number 3.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] and in e-court, it is 4D453. Very well. We have both pages on the screen, both in B/C/S and in English.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Let me ask you this: This is the organisation of the special police brigade, in keeping in the rules dated 5 October 1994, the rules that we have just looked at together. And you have told us that it was part of the police administration or police directorate and the public security sector; wouldn't that be correct?

utterances.speaker: MLADEN BAJAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Can you now help us to understand this schematic better. Could you please tell us what we can see on the left-hand side of the schematic?

utterances.speaker: MLADEN BAJAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: We can see the whole schematic of the special police brigade organisation. On the left-hand side, you can see the command in the large square with all the personnel and officials that make up such a command. In keeping with the law and rules, these people are or these officials are commander, deputy commander, assistant commander for operational tasks, assistant commander for intelligence and security, assistant commander for operational work and teaching, assistant commander for logistics, head of communications, and other professionals and technical staff that belong to the staff according to the job specification of the command.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: In order to help us understand this schematic better, there are three more rectangular areas that are attached to the command. Can you please explain?

utterances.speaker: MLADEN BAJAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. These represent, first, the teaching and instruction team on the two logistical support team; and under 3, communication or signal section.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Very well then. Now I would kindly ask you to explain for us the right-hand part of this schematic. The title is "Special Police Detachments."

utterances.speaker: MLADEN BAJAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: According to the rules that were in effect at the time, special police detachments were as follows: Sarajevo, Sekovici, Bilice, Bijeljina, Doboj, Banja Luka, and Prijedor. At that moment, the special police brigade had seven special police detachments.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Very well. I believe that we will no longer need this document. I would like us to look at the document under tab 19 in your binder.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This document is P54.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: While we are waiting for the document to appear in e-court, maybe we could just briefly analyse it. Could you please tell us, in the left upper corner, it says: "Republika Srpska, Minister of the Interior, Special Police Brigade, Bijeljina" and the date is 20 February 1995. Could you please tell us, under RE, what is the document about?

utterances.speaker: MLADEN BAJAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The special police brigade in this document addresses the top of the Ministry of the Interior, and provides comments under rules on the job specification in the Republika Srpska MUP with regard to the special police brigade.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: We will not dwell upon too long on the document; it will be further analysed through another schematic. However, based on this document, would you be able to tell us it depicts more aspects that are depicted in the job specification; isn't that correct?

utterances.speaker: MLADEN BAJAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The command of the special police brigade informs the Ministry of the Interior about the mistakes and omissions in the book of rules that had already been passed, and provides a clear guidelines how things should look in the book of rules with regard to the actual situation on the ground. In view of that --

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: I apologise for interrupting you --

utterances.speaker: MLADEN BAJAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In view of that, we can see that nine special police detachments are mentioned in this document, as opposed to what we have just seen as the existence of seven different police detachments, which I can list.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: No, that will not be necessary. We will look at the schematic that you prepared, and I believe that it will provide a good explanation of the reasons for this mistake. It is your binder tab 16, page 7?

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] And in e-court, it is 4D454, or document number 4.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: This is the schematic of the organisation of the special police brigade that was in place in July 1995. We can see it in your schematic. It was drafted based on the comments provided on the 20th of February 1995, which is precisely the document that we have just seen in e-court; wouldn't that be correct.

utterances.speaker: MLADEN BAJAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Could you please explain the schematic that we are looking at, at the moment?

utterances.speaker: MLADEN BAJAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Just like the previous schematic, this one also depicts, on the left-hand side, the composition of the special police brigade command, starting with the commander to the technical and professional staff, as well as the three units that belong to the command: Education and structure, communication section, logistics platoon. Obviously, in the centre, or to the right-hand side, with regard to what we have just mentioned, we can see the list of the then-existing special police brigade detachments.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Can you please answer --

utterances.speaker: MLADEN BAJAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: What is listed --

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: I apologise.

utterances.speaker: MLADEN BAJAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The special detachments that are listed are or Jahorina, Sekovici, Bilice, Bijeljina, Doboj, Banja Luka, Prijedor, Ilidza, and Srbinje.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Very well.

utterances.speaker: MLADEN BAJAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: And as I have listed them, that was numerical denotation, starting with Jahorina being the first special detachment, to Srbinje being the ninth special detachment.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: From 1 to 9?

utterances.speaker: MLADEN BAJAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, from 1 to 9.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Very well. Now I would like us to look at the following schematic, which is attached to the expert report. It is page 8 under tab 16.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It is schematic number 5. The Exhibit number in e-court is 4D455. We believe that we have the document in e-court in both languages.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: I would just like to clarify this schematic. This is the organisation of a specific police detachment which was in place in July 1995, pursuant to the Rule 108 1/94 that we have already discussed. In other words, this the schematic of the special police detachment, as posed to the previous schematic that depicted the organisation of the special police brigade?

utterances.speaker: MLADEN BAJAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Tell me, please, what is on the left-hand side of this schematic?

utterances.speaker: MLADEN BAJAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is the schematic of the special police detachment with the structure of the command of the special police detachment on the left-hand side of the schematic. The command is supposed of the commander, the deputy commander, an assistant for intelligence and security, a logistics assistant, as well as the communications squad.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Very well. You have also provided us with the direct line of communication [as interpreted] leading from the command rightwards towards the platoons?

utterances.speaker: MLADEN BAJAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. The special police detachment has four platoons which are also known as special platoons: A special platoon, a mechanized armour platoon, a fire support platoon, and a logistics support platoon.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Very well. I apologise. I will interrupt you just for a moment in order to correct something in the transcript.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] There is an error that should be taken care of immediately. [In English] On page 48, it's line 16. It's "line of command," instead of "line of communication."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Lazarevic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I apologise, Professor. Let's go back to where I interrupted you. Could you please tell us about the platoons. Could you please repeat the names of the platoons within a special police detachment?

utterances.speaker: MLADEN BAJAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As I already told you, there were four platoons. We can see semi-circle lines because every platoon has a commander, and circular arrows or curved arrows point to the first, second, and third squad of the special platoon. Within the mechanised armoured platoon, there are four squads in total. Within the fire support platoon, there are three squads. And, finally, the logistics support platoon has three squad and a service squad or department that was support to that platoon.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: In order to finalise this subject relating to the special police brigade, one question more before we move to the PJPs: Tell me, in 1995, did the special police brigade have a staff of its own?

utterances.speaker: MLADEN BAJAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, it didn't. As we can see from all the charts and what is stipulated by the law and the set of rules, the special police brigade, or the SPB, had a command, and we saw who the members of the commands were, and it had detachments. There was no staff within the SPB.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Thank you very much. I'm sorry. Are you feeling well?

utterances.speaker: MLADEN BAJAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Everything is all right.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Everything is okay. Can I see the 65 ter 4D454 again. I wanted to ask this question because the witness said that in relation to the previous schematic, 453, which depicts the system in 1994, he said that at that time special police brigade was within the police directorate within this public security department; but by this time, by 1995, the special police brigade has become subordinated directly to the MUP. I wanted to be clear about this.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: By all means, Your Honour. I will try to clarify this. Can we have 4D450.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Bajagic, in order to remove any dilemmas from our mind, in this chart that we saw before, this represents the organisational chart existing in July 1995; and on the left-hand side -- I'm sorry. This is 1C in your report, 450.

utterances.speaker: MLADEN BAJAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can see it.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: In accordance with this chart, the SPB is directly in the office of the minister; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MLADEN BAJAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. In July 1995, the SPB belonged to the office of the minister at the ministry headquarters. It was not within the public security department and police administration. That was the situation that is existed before.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Therefore it was directly subordinated to the minister?

utterances.speaker: MLADEN BAJAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. The SPB was directly subordinated to the Ministry of the Interior.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: By all means.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you, Judge Kwon, and thank you, Mr. Lazarevic and Professor. Let's go on.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Bajagic, let us now move on to the subject of PJPs. In your report, you have cited as a legal basis for the establishment of PJP Articles 24, 31 -- and 31 of the Law on Internal Affairs of the 15th of April 1992. This is 4D212. That's document number 1 in your binder. First of all, let us look at Article 31 of this law.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That's on page 4 of the B/C/S version and on page 8 of the English version.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'm sorry.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: I am sorry, tab 1. Do you have it before you?

utterances.speaker: MLADEN BAJAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: So, in Article number 31, if we look at the first paragraph of this article, I don't want to go into a detailed analysis, but what I would like to note about this first paragraph is that I would like to hear who is authorised to engage the PJPs for a specific task and duties?

utterances.speaker: MLADEN BAJAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Pursuant to Article 31, if the interest of public order and security demands so, the minister shall demand the formation of certain -- of police units made up of members of other sections. That is what I mentioned in paragraph 142 of my expert report. That was one of the legal bases for establishing the PJPs.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Can we now look at the exhibit that we've already seen at your tab number 14. That's the rules on internal organisation of MUP, dated the 1st of April 1994. I'm specifically interested in Rule 10 of these rules.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That's Exhibit 4D144; page 9 in e-court in B/C/S, and page 3 in English. This is the translation provided by the defence since we haven't yet received an official translation from the CLSS.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Can you see Article 10 before you?

utterances.speaker: MLADEN BAJAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I can.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Let's look at what it lays down and stipulates. Tell us exactly what precisely this article provides for, and let's begin with paragraph 1.

utterances.speaker: MLADEN BAJAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Paragraph 1 of Article 10 says that public security centres and public security stations for the purpose of neutralizing sabotage and terrorist groups and for participating in combat activities, when necessitated, special police units will be established made up of active duty policemen from the wartime structure.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Pursuant to paragraph 2 of this Article 10, who is the one to decide the strengths and the composition of PJP units?

utterances.speaker: MLADEN BAJAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is to be decided by the Minister of the Interior. He is responsible on the basis of a special or separate decision as it is stipulated in paragraph 2.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: According to this article, the PJP is made by active duty policemen and wartime formation --

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Article 15 on pages 10 and 11 in B/C/S -- I apologise. That's in e-court on page 10 and in the English version it is on page 3 -- or rather 4.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Let's look at the last paragraph of Article 15. Can you see it?

utterances.speaker: MLADEN BAJAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I can.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: We can also see here somewhere in the middle of this --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreters would kindly ask the counsel to slow down, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Let's move on to Article 47 of this book of rules. This is page 34 in e-court, page 5 in the English translation.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Do you see Article 47 in front of you?

utterances.speaker: MLADEN BAJAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Let's now look at paragraph 2 -- or rather, paragraph 1, which should be paragraph 2 of Article 47, which starts with special units. Could you please tell us what you see written in there?

utterances.speaker: MLADEN BAJAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It says here that special police units are commanded by the commander of the unit in the centre, and the commander of the special MUP units is in command of the joint units. Do you need any further explanation?

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: I believe that this regulation that we have just quoted is self-explanatory, and there's no need for any further elaboration. Let's just round the thing off. Let's look at the law on the implementation of the Law on the Interior in the situations of the threat of war or imminent threat of war. We have already seen this document. This is under tab 15.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The Exhibit number is 4D413. The page that we are looking for is 4 in B/C/S and page 12 in English.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Do you see Article 12 in this law, please?

utterances.speaker: MLADEN BAJAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Could you please specify what this article defines?

utterances.speaker: MLADEN BAJAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Article 12 defines or sets out that the Minister of the Interior shall establish special police units, in addition to the special police brigade, to carry out combat tasks.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: And the primary reason that is mentioned here are combat tasks?

utterances.speaker: MLADEN BAJAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, the article is clear enough in that respect.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Is this a convenient moment to break because I'm going to another set of documents.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Sure. Let's have a 25 minute break. Thank you. --- Break taken at 12.24 p.m.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Lazarevic, and we need to accelerate a bit.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: I'll do my best, Your Honour. However, I was also advised by the Prosecution that they will reduce their cross-examination because so far they don't see reason for four hours of cross-examination. So we'll be on schedule, I can assure you this.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: But that should be indicative as to why I'm telling you to accelerate.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Dr. Bajagic, let's move to the documents that follow. In your tab 21, there's Exhibit 4D213, the order to establish PJP, dated 12 September 1994.

utterances.speaker: MLADEN BAJAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Following the instructions of the president of the Chamber, I'd like to make a few points relative to this document. Let's look at item 4 of this order. Can you tell us within whose jurisdiction --

utterances.speaker: MLADEN BAJAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Item 4 says that it's the Minister of the Interior, or his deputy, are authorised to approve the use of PJP.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Can we turn to page 2 of this document. It's item 6. Tell us, what does it say?

utterances.speaker: MLADEN BAJAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Item 6 says that members of the PJP, when not engaged in the execution of combat tasks, shall perform their regular duties as an organisational unit of the MUP.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Let us look at this attachment to the order to establish PJP. It's document under tab 22, and it's 4D214.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Can we have the next page of this document, excuse me. First, I would like to see page number 2 and then page number 1.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Dr. Bajagic, we have the document on the screen now, but I'd like to make sure that you have the same document before you. It's an organogram where it says "PJP, 5712."

utterances.speaker: MLADEN BAJAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do have it.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: This organogram was attached to the document we looked at previously. Can you tell us, really very briefly, how is the structure of the PJP shown here?

utterances.speaker: MLADEN BAJAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's the overall organisation of PJP. It shows there are four brigades of special units of the police, and it shows the structure of the brigades themselves, how many battalions they have, together with their sections of support and communications.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: I won't spend much time on this document. Can we now see page 1 of the same document. It's also an organogram.

utterances.speaker: MLADEN BAJAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: We can't see all of it on the screen. It's the structure of PJP Zvornik. Just tell us about the structure as shown here?

utterances.speaker: MLADEN BAJAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is a detailed schematic of the PJP Zvornik with its command, and we see that PJP Zvornik had four companies, one support platoon, and one communication section; and then we see the breakdown of various companies with their commands and platoons.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: All right. I think we are finished with this document. We don't need to go into details. Let us look at the next document related to the previous one. In 4D213, it said that the way -- the manner of usage shall be prescribed by a separate instruction, and this now is the instruction on the establishment of the PJP, tab 23.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] As I've already said, it's the instruction on the establishment and use of PJP, dated 12 September 1994, 4D215.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I have it.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Let's wait for it to be called up in e-court. Let us look at the subheading (a), the Establishment of PJP. How does the document defined? How shall PJP be established?

utterances.speaker: MLADEN BAJAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It says: "PJP shall be formed from the combat complement of the Ministry of the Interior." It defines the criteria and the requirements for members and certain other matters, such as levels of responsibility within the PJP.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Fine. Let us look at subheading(b) where it says "Use of the PJP." What does paragraph 1 stipulate?

utterances.speaker: MLADEN BAJAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Paragraph 1 stipulates that orders to use PJP shall be given through the PJP commander by the Minister of the Interior or his deputy.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: What about paragraph 2? It is concerns the use of PJP. Can you tell us how this instruction defines it?

utterances.speaker: MLADEN BAJAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Two tasks of the PJP are defined here in detail. It says: "The PJP will be used for the execution of combat tasks and complex police duties within the scope of MUP activities."

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: So the PJP is not used exclusively for combat?

utterances.speaker: MLADEN BAJAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. You can see it from this document and from reality, complex police tasks from the jurisdiction of the MUP imply what they imply, and they do not mean combat activities.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Can we just look at the next page of this document, the second paragraph. What powers are given to the chief of the public security centre?

utterances.speaker: MLADEN BAJAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The chief of the public security centre may allow the use of PJP at the level of his open centre, if so required by the circumstances, and if the situation and the timing does not allow any consultation with the minister. That means in situations that qualify as emergency.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Now let us look at what the procedure for using PJP was like in practice. I would like to look at P13 [sic]. In your binder, it's tab 69. In the second binder, it's tab 69.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: That's not the right document. I apologise. It's P31. Sorry. Yes, that's the right one.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] To speed things up, I'll say what this document is about. It's a dispatch from the Main Staff of the Army of Republika Srpska, the intelligence and security sector. The date is 19 March 1995, and the author of this document is indicated as assistant commander, Major-General Zdravko Tolimir. The subject of the document is indicated as "The establishment of the security system and control of the territory." I had like to go through the important points of this document. Let us look at the addressee.

utterances.speaker: MLADEN BAJAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This dispatch was sent to the president of Republika Srpska, first; to the Ministry of the Interior; and to the state security sector; and the command of the Drina Corps, for their information.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Let us look at paragraph 3. It begins somewhere halfway through the paragraphs with the words "We hereby propose ..." Obviously, it is proposed to use MUP units and it goes from the Main Staff to the president of the republic, and it defines the proposed tasks for the MUP units.

utterances.speaker: MLADEN BAJAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We won't be needing this document anymore. Let us look at the next document. It's 4D --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could counsel repeat which 4D exhibit?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes. The interpreters need you to repeat which 4D document you are referring to.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: It's 4DP6.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Bajagic, this is an order from the president of the republic, Radovan Karadzic. The date a 21st of March 1995. Can you tell us what is the order?

utterances.speaker: MLADEN BAJAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As we can see from the text, the president of the republic, pursuant to the constitution and the laws, orders that with a view to establishing a regimen of security and control in a given area of the territory, the possibility be considered of stationing certain units in Konjevic Polje.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: In your opinion, is this document related to the previous one we looked at?

utterances.speaker: MLADEN BAJAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Certainly. The previous document was dated 19 March 1995, and this one is dated 21st March 1995.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: The next document I'd like us to look at is document 4DP7. It's in your tab 25.

utterances.speaker: MLADEN BAJAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [No interpretation]

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes. We are not receiving any interpretation, at least I'm not and Judge Prost isn't either.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Bajagic, there seems to be a technical problem with the interpretation. It's fine now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Mr. Lazarevic, it's fixed. Go to line 9, and what we have in the transcript is: "The next document I'd like to look at is document 4DP7. It's in your tab 25." That's where the translation stopped, so you can go ahead from there.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] So, this is a document signed by the Minister of the Interior, Zivko Rakic. It's sent to the President of the Republika Srpska, Dr Radovan Karadzic. The date we see is 23 March 1995, and it references the telegram of 21st March 1995. What does this document say?

utterances.speaker: MLADEN BAJAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This document as we can see says that the Minister of the Interior had followed the order of the president of Republika Srpska, and they inform him that they had sent the 2nd Company of the PJP to the designated area from the public security centre of Zvornik, in order to establish a security regime in control of the territory over the uninhabited parts of the territory, rather.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Do you see any relationship between this and the previous two documents?

utterances.speaker: MLADEN BAJAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Certainly.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Let us look at the next document. It's in your tab 70.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It's P8 in e-court.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: There it is. To speed things up a little, I will analyse this briefly myself. This is an order that the Supreme Commander of the armed forces of Republika Srpska, President Karadzic, sent on the 22nd April 1995 to the Main Staff of the Army of Republika Srpska and to the MUP of Republika Srpska. Let us just see. In the first paragraph, below the words "I hereby order..." what kind of information did President Karadzic have?

utterances.speaker: MLADEN BAJAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In the first paragraph of this order, it says that: "The Main Staff of the army must in the future define more precisely and more specifically requests for engagement and use of MUP units in keeping with the provisions of the law." And in the second paragraph, it says that: "The MUP is required when sending MUP units into combat as part of the Army of Republika Srpska to regulate precisely the responsibilities of the commanding officers and commanders when they are resubordinated to the VRS unit commander."

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: And the last document on this topic is in tab -- under tab 71 in your binder.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It's 4D261.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Have you got it?

utterances.speaker: MLADEN BAJAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: We have it on the screen now. This was sent from the Main Staff of the VRS on the 23rd of April 1995. It was signed, as we can see on page 2, by Chief of Staff Colonel-General Milan Milovanovic. It was sent to the command of the first and 2nd Krajina Corps, Sarajevo Romanija corps, the East Bosnian Corps, the Herzegovina Corps, and the Drina Corps. And since this document contains practically the entire previous document that had been are forwarded to the previous corps, I'd like to look at page 2, the last paragraph.

utterances.speaker: MLADEN BAJAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: What is written in that last paragraph?

utterances.speaker: MLADEN BAJAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Bearing in mind the entire text of this order, where it says in the beginning, with a view to overcoming certain problems and dilemmas, the last paragraph says: In the future follow the order to engage the police units only through the Main Staff of the VRS."

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: That's what Colonel General Milovanovic says, it's not contained in the previous document; right?

utterances.speaker: MLADEN BAJAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Right.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Very well. Thank you very much. And now I'd like to move on to my next topic -- or rather, your next topic in your expert report, and the topic is the training centre on Mount Jahorina. Let's look at document 91 in your binder.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This is 4D212 in e-court; page 7 in English -- I apologise, it will be page 7 in B/C/S, and pages 16 and 17 in English.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: This is Article 63 of the Law on the Internal Affairs.

utterances.speaker: MLADEN BAJAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I've got the document.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Could you please tell us what the article prescribes, Article 63?

utterances.speaker: MLADEN BAJAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Article 63 in chapter 7 of this law says that, in the ministry, there is a training centre for the education of the staff of the ministry of Internal Affairs; and in the seconds paragraph, it says that its task is to prepare and educate personnel to work at the ministry.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Let's move on to Article 65. Could you please tell us what this means?

utterances.speaker: MLADEN BAJAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In its first paragraph, this article says that the centre provides education for the personnel who are earmarked for work at the Ministry of the Interior, and the second paragraph says that the centre also provides education for some other legal persons.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: And let's just look at another short article, which is Article 66. Could you please explain?

utterances.speaker: MLADEN BAJAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: According to Article 66, the centre also has a school for interior and the boarding or a dorm.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: What would be the main function of the education centre, according to these articles?

utterances.speaker: MLADEN BAJAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It would be the education and training, as well as continuous education and specialist education, of the personnel working at the Ministry of the Interior, be it the education and training of the already existing staff or those who intend to join the ministry in the future.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Thank you very much. The next document I would like to show you consists of two consecutive documents. The first one is document -- I apologise, in your binder they are under 26.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The document number is 4D251.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I can see the document.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Very well then. What I would be interested in is the following: You see that this was sent to the special brigade of the police at Jahorina terminal -- actually, this is the sender. Let's now pay attention to the date. The date is 16 April 1995. Let's pay attention to the second part of the second page starting with words "the current agreement."

utterances.speaker: MLADEN BAJAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can see that.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: My question arises from this dispatch. In addition to the trainers and the special police brigade, who else was involved in the training of the participants in the course?

utterances.speaker: MLADEN BAJAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As you can see from this document, in addition to the instructors from the special police brigade, the training course also involved teachers from the school of the interior and the name of the specific teacher is mentioned here as Nedo Sevo, as well as the psychologist Aco Milic from the school. In other words, there were two people involved from the school.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: And just to pinpoint that and attach it to a certain time period, I would like us to look at the first sentence of this document starting with words, "In the evening of 5 February 1995 ..."

utterances.speaker: MLADEN BAJAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I'm with you.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: We would then have to say that this is about the group of trainees who arrived from the CJB Zvornik?

utterances.speaker: MLADEN BAJAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: And the total number of trainees is given at 142?

utterances.speaker: MLADEN BAJAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: The following document I'd like to show you is under number 27, a very brief document in your binder.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] In the e-court system, it is 4D252.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I've got the document in front of me.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Could you please tell us something about this document. This document is a request in view of the problems, the problem being that officers had failed to arrive, and there is a request placed on the staff to send urgently an officer. Could you please explain?

utterances.speaker: MLADEN BAJAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This means that a request is being sent in view of the failure of one officer to arrive, that his replacement should be sent, and the person is specified here, in order to work with the trainees. In other words, a request is made upon the special police brigade to send another person who would be helping with the course.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Let's just summarize the two documents and draw a conclusion based on the two. In addition to the members of the special police brigade who were sent to help with the training, and teachers from the school, what other commitments did the special brigade police have towards this education centre?

utterances.speaker: MLADEN BAJAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as I can tell, the commitment on behalf of the special police brigade was to send a certain number of officers, as previously agreed, who will participate in the implementation of a certain training programme for trainees, together with the teachers from the school.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Thank you very much. We will no longer need this document. In other words, we are talking about a special course for policeman; wouldn't that be correct?

utterances.speaker: MLADEN BAJAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it would.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: The following documents that I would like to look at is under tab 28 in your binder.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This is 4D511.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Let's look at the front page of this document. This is a report on the work of the special police brigade for June 1995. It was drafted in Bijeljina in July 1995, as we can see.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Let's look at page 2 both in the English version as well as in B/C/S.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: You can see, under A, the title, "Statistical overview of days worked in the course of June 1995." The fifth bullet point here is days spent in professional training; 2.413 days is the total sum.

utterances.speaker: MLADEN BAJAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: What would be your interpretation of this particular entry days spent in professional training and the figure that appears next to this?

utterances.speaker: MLADEN BAJAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: My opinion is that this is, as we can see, a very significant number of days. However, a day is compound number of all the days spent at all forms of professional education, of all the members of the special police brigade, which includes education within the brigade as well as any forms of training or education that was provided to the school as courses for future policeman or current policemen. In other words, this is a total sum of all the different educations that I've just mentioned.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: As far as I can understand, this also includes the number of days that members of the special police brigade spent in training as well as the days they spent in training others as instructors?

utterances.speaker: MLADEN BAJAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, you are right.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Very well. Let's look at the following document which is connecting with this one. This is your tab 29.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Exhibit number 4D95 [as interpreted].

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, I have it.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: So this is a report on the work of the SPB in the period January-September 1995; but underneath, it says that the report refers to the period between 1st of January 1995 and 15th October 1995, and the date in the upper left corner is 4th of November 1995.

utterances.speaker: MLADEN BAJAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I see.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Let's look at page 2; and towards the bottom of this page, it also says number spent in training, 32.772. Can you see that?

utterances.speaker: MLADEN BAJAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I can.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Does this basically confirm your conclusion?

utterances.speaker: MLADEN BAJAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it does. It confirms what I said earlier, and this is nine and a half months. That is the aggregate number of days over nine months that members of the SPB spent in training, and the previous document related only to one month.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Very well. The trainees at the training centre, what kind of obligations did they have vis-a-vis the Ministry of the Interior?

utterances.speaker: MLADEN BAJAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Once you become a candidate or a trainee policeman and you attend a course, you undertake an obligation, first and foremost, to attend the training regularly, to attend classes regularly, to behave properly in accordance with the rules of service, and all other things that involve this kind of special training and education.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Let us now look at the next document. That's your tab 30 in your binder.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That's 4D253. It's a dispatch dated -- I am sorry, a dispatch that is 13/95, dated 9th of April 1995.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: It is addressed to the office of the minister as well as to the police forces staff, and so on and so forth. Let us only look at one sentence from this document, which begins: "On 8th April 1995 ..."

utterances.speaker: MLADEN BAJAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I can see that.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: And here see the names of some 15 trainees who left without permission?

utterances.speaker: MLADEN BAJAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: And the next sentence begins in that respect. Can you tell me what was suggested and proposed to do?

utterances.speaker: MLADEN BAJAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The suggestion or the proposal was made that certain measures be taken against these trainees, and the staff wanted feedback information about what other measures were taken with respect to other trainees, whether this would involve disciplinary measures or things like that. I'm now talking about those who left the course without permission.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Let's look at the next document which is in your tab 67.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That's Exhibit 4D358; page 8 in B/C/S, and page 19 in English.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: We already seen this, but I would like to focus on Article 83 of this law, and I would like to hear your comments.

utterances.speaker: MLADEN BAJAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Did you say tab 67?

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Yes, tab 67, and Article 83 of the law. Can you please look at it.

utterances.speaker: MLADEN BAJAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: What does Article 83 provide?

utterances.speaker: MLADEN BAJAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Article 83 provides for the following: If a participant in the course for policemen willfully leaves the course, is expelled from the course because of his own fault, fails to complete the course successfully, is bound to refund the costs of the course -- or rather, the proportionate amount of the course, which means that if a person has established a certain relationship with the ministry, this person is bound to refund the money to the ministry.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Is this document in some way related to the previous document?

utterances.speaker: MLADEN BAJAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Probably. The previous document is based op this by requesting that report be submitted about what measures have been taken, and whether they have been taken at all in compliance with Article 83, when it refers to those who willfully left the course.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Thank you very much. The next document that I would like us to look at is in your tab 31.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This is Exhibit P726. This is an order issued by the commander chief addressed to all ministries and the government of RS, presidents of municipalities, and the Main Staff of the VRS. It bears the date of 16th June 1995.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: As I said, this is an order, and this document has already been analysed during this trial. I'm particularly interested in item 3 of this document, paragraph 2 or subitem (2). Can you tell me what it contains?

utterances.speaker: MLADEN BAJAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Item 3 of this order, subitem (2), says that the Ministries of Defence and of Interior shall undertake necessary actions for the return of conscripts from the Federal Republic of Yugoslavia and their recruitment in the units of the armed forces.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Let's look now at the next document. That's -- just a second. It's your tab 15. So this is the law on the implementation of the Law on Army during a state of imminent threat of war or a state of war.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That's Exhibit 4D413; page 3 in B/C/S and page 7 in English.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Can we look at Article 12 of this law, please.

utterances.speaker: MLADEN BAJAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Which law?

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: I am sorry. That's law on the implementation of the Law on the Army in the state the immediate threat of war or state of war.

utterances.speaker: MLADEN BAJAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I have it; Article 12.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Can you just tell us what this Article 12 governs?

utterances.speaker: MLADEN BAJAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This article governs -- the deployment of reserve forces to the army is to be carried out by the ministry of Defence. So the obligation of the Ministry of Defence would be to deploy military conscripts.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Based on the documents that you had an opportunity to go through, and based on these regulations, what would happen to those conscripts once they completed their training?

utterances.speaker: MLADEN BAJAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, once military conscripts completed their training as prescribed, they are supposed to be assigned to the armed forces of Republika Srpska, and we know which of these two forces we are talking about.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: And just one more document before we finish for today. That's your tab 32 in folder 1.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That's Exhibit 4D300. So this is a letter sent by Tomislav Kovac, the deputy minister to the president of the Republika Srpska. It's dated the 23rd of June 1995.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Let us just look at the first paragraph.

utterances.speaker: MLADEN BAJAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I see it.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: What can you tell us based on this first paragraph? How many conscripts have been handed over to the VRS?

utterances.speaker: MLADEN BAJAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The deputy minister informs hereby the president of Republika Srpska that from the reception centre in Janja, 1.586 conscripts were delivered to the VRS, out of which 149 conscripts were handed over to the MUP staff in Jahorina.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Is this document in any way related to the order of the commander in chief we have seen a minute ago?

utterances.speaker: MLADEN BAJAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Precisely so, indeed. Within mobilisation affairs, both the Ministry of Defence and the Ministry of the Interior have certain obligations.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Dr. Bajagic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you. We'll adjourn for today, resuming tomorrow at 9.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Wednesday, the 8th day of October, 2008, at 9.00 a.m.

procedural_notes.text: --- Whereupon the hearing adjourned at 1.44 p.m.
